name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,448

clue.text: Document about small rope

blocks.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand for 'concerning'
a cord is a thin rope

explanation.surface: A clerk files paperwork concerning a short length of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something is to put it down in writing, so both words mean set down officially.

clue.text: Dance half of dance with pudding

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only one of its two parts, here the back end of the Latin dance named just before

blocks.note: the rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance
the tail end of the same dance name, rumba, taken again

explanation.surface: A dancer pauses halfway through a dance to grab some pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'dance' is the same rumba, of which only its final pair of letters is kept; 'half' is loose here.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum baba is a small yeast sponge cake soaked in rum syrup, served as a dessert.

clue.text: Rusty tack destabilised ship

indicators.note: something destabilised is knocked out of its settled order, so the preceding words get rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A corroded fastening has made a vessel unstable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cutty Sark is a famous nineteenth-century tea clipper preserved in dry dock at Greenwich, London.

clue.text: During bumpy ride, swan came to maturity

indicators.note: a bumpy journey jolts things about, so the letters of the ride are jumbled
during places one thing inside the time span of another, so the bird goes within

blocks.note: the letters of ride rearranged
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: On a rough boat trip, a swan grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is the female swan (the male is a cob), a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or ideas that have ripened have developed fully, reaching full growth or readiness.

clue.text: Obama upset about Republican's second-lowest life form

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the president's name is rearranged
second points to the letter in position two of the party word
about means surrounding, so the jumbled name goes round the chosen letter

blocks.note: the former US president's name rearranged
the letter in second place of the word

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a Republican is the lowest form of life, and Obama is upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This single-celled protozoan is the stock example of the most primitive kind of organism.

clue.text: Cry for help in publicity about end of democracy welcomed by PM

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word that follows
about here means turned round, so the combined advert and letter run backwards
something welcomed by a host is taken inside, so the prime minister's name surrounds the rest

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
the closing letter of democracy
Theresa May, UK prime minister 2016 to 2019

explanation.surface: A political lament: the prime minister presides over democracy's end amid spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was a British prime minister; her surname wraps round the reversed pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayday is the international radio distress call used by ships and aircraft in grave danger.

clue.text: Get rid of cream containing minute angelica root

indicators.note: a root is where a plant starts, so the opening letter of the herb is taken
containing means holding inside, so the word for cream wraps the other pieces

blocks.note: the cream is the best, the elite
min is the abbreviation for minute
the opening letter of angelica

explanation.surface: A cookery tip: discard cream that has a tiny bit of angelica root in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Angelica is a herb whose candied stems decorate cakes, which suits the kitchen surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove or exclude it completely, a direct synonym for discarding.

clue.text: Frail men talking about complaint

indicators.note: about here means lying around within, so the letters sit inside the preceding run of words

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: Elderly, weak men chatting about their health problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or minor disorder, a standard synonym.

clue.text: Painter with strange new desire to protect 22

indicators.note: strange suggests something out of its usual form, so the following letters are reordered
to protect something is to surround it, so the jumbled letters go round the cross-referenced word

blocks.note: the letters of the two words rearranged
the answer to 22 across is estate, and an estate is land

explanation.surface: An artist feels an odd new urge to look after a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 refers to 22 across, ESTATE, here a synonym for land.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian artist famous for animal paintings and the Trafalgar Square lions.

clue.text: Dirty mark made by small dog with no tail

indicators.note: with no tail means the end is cut off, so the dog word loses its final letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A little dog leaves a muddy stain on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is a flake of soot or a dark smudge, so it names a small sooty stain.

clue.text: Tantrum leading to troubled life on Dutch agricultural land

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed and unsettled, so the letters of the next word are stirred up

blocks.note: a paddy is British slang for a fit of temper
the letters of life rearranged
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A fit of rage leads to a hard life on a Dutch farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy for a temper tantrum is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy field is a flooded plot where rice is grown, a type of farmland.

clue.text: Clergyman burying Yorick's head in ravine

indicators.note: the head of a name is its opening letter
burying puts one thing inside another, so the churchman holds the letter

blocks.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral's clergy
the opening letter of Yorick

explanation.surface: A churchman buries the skull of Yorick, Hamlet's jester, in a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Yorick's skull in Hamlet, so 'head' looks literal but means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge with steep sides, so it is a large kind of ravine.

clue.text: Pictures in one book of maps taken from periodicals

indicators.note: taken from means removed out of, so the map book is lifted out of the word for periodicals

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
magazines are periodical publications
the A–Z is the standard British street atlas

explanation.surface: A single atlas full of pictures is pulled from a stack of magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: The A–Z is a British book of street maps; removing it from MAGAZINES leaves MAGINES.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, so pictures as a verb matches.

clue.text: Plant found by pacifists drinking beer at university city

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the pacifist group's letters swallow the drink

blocks.note: the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, a British peace movement
ale is a kind of beer
U is the abbreviation for university
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Peace protesters having a pint at a college town spot a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: CND, the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, is Britain's best-known anti-nuclear group.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendula is the marigold genus, a flowering garden and medicinal herb.

clue.text: Spoil cape maybe belonging to a bishop

indicators.note: maybe signals one possible version among several, so the letters may be arranged another way

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone may ruin a cloak that belongs to a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal derives from the Greek for overseer, the root of bishop, and describes a bishop's office.

clue.text: Dunce finally excluded from class project

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
excluded from means left out of, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the closing letter of dunce
a caste is a social class

explanation.surface: A slow pupil is thrown out of a school assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' looks like a noun for schoolwork, but it is the verb meaning to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to throw or hurl forward, as one casts a line or a stone.

clue.text: Eastern ruler's poem rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read the other way

blocks.note: a rime is an old spelling of rhyme, a poem, as in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern monarch's verse has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim prince or commander, a title of rulers in the Middle East.

clue.text: Drain top of ulcer in Texas hospital complex

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its opening letter
complex means intricately tangled, so all these letters are rearranged together

blocks.note: the opening letter of ulcer
taken as written
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A doctor lances an ulcer in a Texan medical complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' reads as a noun for a hospital campus, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain someone or something is to use up all its strength or contents, the same as exhaust.

clue.text: Sloth featured in handout found in pub next to church

indicators.note: something featured in a place appears inside it, so the handout goes within the pub

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
the dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Laziness shows up in the benefit claimant drinking in a pub by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next to' just places the church letters after the pub; 'the dole' is British for unemployment pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth, one of the seven deadly sins, is laziness or idleness, which is what indolence means.

clue.text: Supervise part of match on court

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls, a section of play
a see is a bishop's seat, and the Holy See is the papal court

explanation.surface: A referee keeps an eye on one stage of a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests tennis, but it is the Holy See, the Pope's court. In a down clue, A on B puts A above B.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct work, a direct synonym for supervising it.

clue.text: Company linked to closure of Stormont upset Ireland's charmed circle

indicators.note: closure of means the end, so the final letter is taken
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
the closing letter of Stormont
Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Political news: Stormont, Northern Ireland's parliament, shuts and upsets an inner clique.
explanation.walkthrough: Stormont is the seat of the Northern Ireland Assembly in Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group with shared interests, often called a charmed circle.

clue.text: Pressure on singers to hold new nationalist flag

indicators.note: to hold means to keep inside, so the opera company surrounds the letter for new

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
the English National Opera
N is the abbreviation for new
N is the abbreviation for nationalist

explanation.surface: A nationalist banner gets singers to raise a flag under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: ENO, English National Opera, is London's national opera company. In a down clue, P 'on' ENO puts it above.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow pointed flag, as once carried on a knight's lance.

clue.text: Draughts in politician's house reported

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the house name counts

blocks.note: Chequers is the British prime minister's country residence in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: There are cold air currents in a politician's home, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draughts' suggests cold air, but it is the board game. Chequers is the British PM's official country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkers is the American name for the board game the British call draughts.

clue.text: Electronic voice in car?

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
to voice an opinion is to state it

explanation.surface: A satnav or electronic assistant speaking from inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: an estate is one type of car.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is the British name for a station wagon, a car with an extended rear load area.

clue.text: Turned up remains containing a shocking weapon

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the remains word wraps the article
turned up in a down clue means flipped to read from the bottom, so the result runs backwards

blocks.note: the rest is what remains
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remains are dug up with an alarming weapon among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like an opinion, but it is literal: the weapon delivers an electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a stun gun firing darts that deliver an electric shock, so a weapon that shocks.

clue.text: Posters about defining feature of lingerie

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for posters goes round the marketing term

blocks.note: people who post letters are senders
a USP is a unique selling point, a product's defining feature

explanation.surface: Advertising posters discuss what makes some underwear distinctive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posters' reads as billboards, but it means people who post things.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspenders, the straps holding up stockings in British usage, are an item of lingerie.

clue.text: See 2
Money in fiction books

blocks.note: a tale is a story, a piece of fiction
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: There is money to be made in writing novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money' looks like a word for skill's reward, but a talent was an ancient unit of weight and currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent was a large sum of silver or gold used as currency in the ancient world, as in the biblical parable.

clue.text: Learn to service empty vehicle

indicators.note: empty means the inside is cleared out, leaving just the outer letters of the word

blocks.note: to hear news is to learn it
only the outer letters of service

explanation.surface: Instructions to learn how to maintain an unoccupied vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'service' that hints at funerals sits beside the hearse in the surface, though it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin to a funeral.
